expectation: ADH will cause the ducts to return more water to the blood.

reaction: The concentration difference makes the water movement clearer.

reaction: The physical route from nerve endings to blood is clear.
reason: The body needs the newly built hormone route for water control.

reaction: The return toward the usual range provides a satisfying close to the water-control sequence.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting ADH to collecting-duct water recovery was most worthwhile: the planned diagram links receptors, extra water channels and the surrounding concentration difference to reduced water loss in urine.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building and then attaching the hormone route repeated a connection already introduced in the sensor-to-ADH sequence, although it clarified the physical anatomy.

surprise.text: The final illustration plan showed fewer ADH signals as plasma concentration approached its usual range, adding a feedback connection beyond simply replacing lost water.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though assembling a separate nerve-ending and blood-vessel route after ADH had already been released felt somewhat repetitive.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the water-channel mechanism and the final feedback comparison made the system connections interesting, despite some repetitive assembly. ADH was not spelled out in the supplied chapter, which could leave students uncertain about the term.
